frames.narration: A new instance is starting. It is loading its cache, so the readiness check fails. The load balancer does not send it any traffic yet.
The cache is loaded. The readiness check passes, and the load balancer adds the instance to the pool.
Later the application deadlocks. The process is running, but it no longer answers. The liveness check times out repeatedly.
After three failures in a row, the orchestrator restarts the instance. The load balancer meanwhile stops sending it requests. Users hit the other instances.
Now the database has a one-minute outage. If the readiness check includes the database, every instance fails readiness at the same moment...
...and the load balancer removes all of them. No instance can serve even the requests that do not need the database. A short blip becomes a complete outage.

Better: readiness only checks the instance itself. The instances stay in the pool, requests that need the database fail fast through a circuit breaker, and everything else keeps working until the database returns.
